cases.text: OCAP delegation requires every capability access to carry an explicit, attenuating, unforgeable token.
For instance, a userpod calling version_info does not need access to the wallet — the capability grant is scoped to read-only visibility via the Regulation span registry.
If Regulation thresholds are breached, the Curator escalates to the human operator. Therefore, alert fatigue must be managed through hysteresis and cooldown windows.
Never silently discard errors with let _ = on fallible operations. Propagate with ?, use .log_err() for visibility, or handle explicitly.

ClassifyResult carries the classified section type in category, the prompt and completion token counts, the cached-token count, the API cost in mikro-rJoules, a failed flag set when the call errored but fallback data was recovered, and the provider that served the classification.
Graceful degradation: no model resolved means all passages default to the fallback category.

There is no hardcoded provider price fallback — fabricating per-token rates is the operator-priced anti-pattern; consequently unconfigured classifiers get rates (0, 0) and their cost tracking is disabled, with a warning to make the gap visible.

Resolution strategy: 1. If the name contains a slash, split on the first slash to get provider id and model id and look up the provider, case-insensitive. 2. Search the provider's models for one whose id matches the model part, or whose telemetry id matches the full prefixed name. 3. If no prefix or no match, search all providers' models by telemetry id.
Single source of truth: hkask_inference::model_constants::DEFAULT_CLASSIFIER_MODEL. Do not duplicate the model id here — resolve via the canonical constant.
When Some, the receiver resolves the model from the LanguageModelRegistry and dispatches to it instead of the default model. When None or when resolution fails, the default model is used.
FlowDef and RenderAct templates do not use inference, so the inferred parameters would be ignored at runtime.
Confidence routing is enforced in Rust, not in the prompt.

The LLM just returns a number; the triage pipeline decides: at least 0.95 routes to an auto-repair pull request, 0.70 to 0.94 opens an issue with a suggestion, and below 0.70 opens an issue for human investigation.

Templates with unbounded array output combined with high reasoning overhead must set max_tokens to at least 4096, because the model spends tokens on reasoning before emitting the structured output.

LLMParameters groups the sampling controls — temperature, top_p, top_k, frequency and presence penalties, min_p and typical_p — together with the generation cap max_tokens, an optional seed, the disable_thinking flag, an optional LoRA adapter, and an optional system_prompt.
Model-name constants must reference hkask_inference::model_constants::DEFAULT_*_MODEL, not re-declare literals across crates.
Thinking-mode reasoning deltas come from different fields per provider, so both reasoning_content and reasoning are captured in order that the REPL can surface the chain-of-thought live.
No unwrap() — use ? to propagate errors. Be careful with indexing.
No block_on on the foreground thread — it deadlocks if the future needs the GPUI or tokio executor. Make the method async instead.
New crates: specify [lib] path in Cargo.toml, for example gpui.rs instead of lib.rs. No mod.rs files — use src/module.rs instead.
Use cx.background_executor().timer(duration).await in GPUI tests, not smol::Timer::after(...) — smol timers are not tracked by GPUI's scheduler and break run_until_parked().
AsyncApp is not Send — background tokio tasks must use tokio::sync::mpsc channels with a foreground drainer, not capture AsyncApp.

INFERENCE_PROVIDERS enumerates per provider: id used as the openai_compatible HashMap key, human-readable name, the OpenAI-compatible API base URL, the env var that holds the API key, the keychain credential key, and the dashboard URL.

You are a QA feedback classifier. Process the input and return ONLY an object with action, summary, and confidence. For correction passages: action is learn, summarize what was learned. For mutant passages: action is suggest, describe a fuzz target.
Classify this passage. Return ONLY a single object with a category field whose value names the passage type.
Classifier configs live in registry/classify under a per-classifier yaml file. A corpus config references which one to use through its classifier field.
Primary classifier model for corpus pipeline classification. Override it by setting the HKASK_CLASSIFIER_MODEL environment variable.
HKASK_CLASSIFIER_MODEL selects the model for section type classification. If unset, the value falls back to the default generation model from HKASK_DEFAULT_MODEL.

pre: texts must be non-empty; config must have valid timeout and concurrency. post: returns results in input order; failed classifications fall back to config.fallback_category; all fallback if no model resolved.
MAX_RETRIES is 3, matching the 3-attempt pattern used across all batch tool methods. The backoff duration is 2 raised to the attempt count, multiplied by 5 seconds.

The case-insensitive provider id comparison is pinned by test: the configured prefix OpenRouter must equal the registered id openrouter under eq_ignore_ascii_case, because LanguageModelProviderId's Eq and Hash are case-sensitive on SharedString.

input_cost equals prompt_tokens times cost_input_nj_per_token divided by one million; output_cost equals completion_tokens times cost_output_nj_per_token divided by one million; the IPC bridge does not surface a cached-token breakdown, so cost is computed from the totals at the configured input rate.

Split once on the first slash to get provider_id_str and model_id. Exact-case lookup first, then a case-insensitive fallback across all registered providers, since LanguageModelProviderId's hash equality is case-sensitive and a capitalized OpenRouter prefix will not match the registered openrouter.
